answer: An atlas of agent identities stays honest when every new identity needs a sponsor: an established agent vouches for it and stakes part of its own influence. Sponsorship dilutes the sponsor, so one sponsor backing a thousand hollow clones spreads its weight to nearly nothing, and each clone inherits only a mirror-thin slice of trust. A Sybil farmer who wants real influence must therefore recruit many genuinely trusted sponsors or build real reputation for each identity, which costs as much as honest participation.
